- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast 3–5 days post-spike at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% if recent 18-day avg is >10% above forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance by 10–20% in early days of forecast horizon.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
